Surah 68: Al-Qalam (The Pen), Makkiyyah

[In manuscript "B" it is Madaniyyah. Ibn al-Durays narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "Whenever the opening of a surah was revealed in Makkah, it was written in Makkah. Then Allah added to it what He willed. The first of the Qur'an to be revealed was (Read in the name of your Lord), then (Al-Muzzammil), then (Al-Muddaththir)." And al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "Surah (Nun. By the pen) was revealed in Makkah." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/240.] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Nun﴾ They differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the fish upon whose back is the earth. This is also the view of Mujahid, Muqatil, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi [Perhaps none of these views is sound regarding the interpretation of Nun as the fish upon which rest the seven earths, or that it is the inkwell, or that it is a tablet of light, or that it is the last letter of the name al-Rahman, or that it is a river of Paradise. See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/307. Ruh al-Ma'ani of al-Alusi: 29/23.].

Abu Zabyan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The first thing Allah created was the pen, and it ran with what would be until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the Nun and spread the earth upon its back, and the Nun moved, so the earth shook. It was then steadied with the mountains, and the mountains boast over the earth." Then Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾ [Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/307, al-Tabari: 29/14, and al-Hakim: 2/498, who authenticated it. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/240-241 added its attribution to al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh in "al-'Azamah," al-Bayhaqi in "al-Asma' wa al-Sifat," al-Khatib in his "Tarikh," and al-Diya' in "al-Mukhtarah." It is a statement attributed to Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf).].

They differed about its name. al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: its name is [Ism] [Omitted from "B".] Yahmut. al-Waqidi said: Luyuthaa. Ka'b said: Luwaythaa. And from 'Ali: its name is Balhawth.

The narrators said: When Allah created the earth and split it open, He sent a angel from beneath the Throne, and he descended to the earth until he entered beneath the seven earths and placed them upon his shoulder, one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, extended and grasping the seven earths, until he held them firmly, but there was no place of rest for his feet. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down from Paradise (al-Firdaws) a bull having forty thousand horns and forty thousand legs, and the resting place of the angel's feet was placed on its hump. But his feet did not settle. So Allah took a green ruby from the highest level of Paradise, whose thickness was a five-hundred-year journey, and placed it between the hump of the bull and its ear, and his feet settled upon it. The horns of that bull extend out to the regions of the earth, and its nostrils are in the sea, and it breathes once every day. When it breathes out, the sea rises, and when it draws back its breath, the sea recedes. The bull's legs had no place of rest, so [Fa-khalaqa] [In "B": fa-ja'ala.] Allah Most High created a rock as thick as the seven heavens and the seven earths, and the bull's legs came to rest upon it. This is the rock about which Luqman said to his son: "O my son, indeed it, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and is within a rock..." But the rock had no place of rest, so Allah created a Nun, which is the great fish, and placed the rock upon its back, while the rest of its body was empty, and the fish was upon the sea, and the sea was upon the back of the wind, and the wind was upon the power. It is said that the whole world with all that is upon it is two letters. The Almighty said to it: [Jalla jalaluhu] [What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".] "Be," and it was.

[This and similar reports, which will follow, are fabrications of the People of the Book who intended to mock the messengers, as Shaykh Muhammad ibn Muhammad Abu Shahbah stated in his book "al-Isra'iliyyat wa al-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir," p. 305. See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/401-402.]

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Iblis slipped into the fish upon whose back rests the earth and whispered to it, saying: "Do you know what is upon your back, O Luwaytha, of nations, animals, trees and mountains? If you shook them off, you would cast them from your back." Luwaytha resolved to do so, but Allah sent a creature which entered its nostril and reached its brain, and the fish cried out to Allah because of it, so Allah permitted it, and it came out. Ka'b said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it looks at it and it looks at it; whenever it intends anything of that, it returns to how it was."

Some said: Nun is the last of the letters of al-Rahman, and this is a narration of 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas.

al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: Nun is the inkwell.

It was also said: it is an oath which Allah swore by. It was said: it is the opening letter of the surah. 'Ata' said: the beginning of its name is light (nur) and helper (nasir).

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by its (the pen's) support for the believers. [al-Tabari transmitted these narrations: 29/15-16.]

﴿And by the pen﴾ [He] [Omitted from "A".] is the one with which Allah wrote the Reminder. It is a pen of light, whose length is the distance between heaven and earth. It is said: the first thing Allah created was the pen, and He looked at it and it split into two halves. Then He said: "Run with what will be until the Day of Resurrection," and it ran upon the Preserved Tablet with that.

﴿And what they inscribe﴾ — yaktubun, "they write": that is, what the recording angels write of the deeds of the children of Adam.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verses 2–4:

﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman.﴾ [HUWA] [[In manuscript "B": "this".]] This is an answer to their saying, "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, you are truly a madman" (al-Hijr 15:6). Then God swore by the letter Nun, by the pen, and by what they write of deeds, and then said: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord,﴾ by the prophethood of your Lord, ﴿a madman.﴾ That is: you are not a madman, and God has blessed you with prophethood and wisdom. It was also said: by the protection (ismah) of your Lord. It was also said: it is like the saying, "You are not a madman," [WA-L-HAMDU LILLAH] [[In manuscript "A": "with the praise of God".]] It was also said: the meaning is, "You are not a madman, and the blessing belongs to your Lord," like their saying, "Glory be to You, O God, and praise," meaning, "and the praise belongs to You."

﴿And indeed for you is a reward never cut off.﴾ That is: not diminished, and not interrupted, for your patience in the face of their slander against you.

﴿And indeed you are of a great character.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: a great religion, no religion is more beloved to me or more pleasing to me than it, and it is the religion of Islam. Al-Hasan said: it is the manners of the Qur'an.

'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she said: "His character was the Qur'an." [[Muslim related it at length in the chapter on the general prayer of the night, in the Book of the Prayer of Travellers and Its Shortening, no. 746, 1/513, from Hakim ibn Aflah, who said to 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her: "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said: "Yes." She said: "The character of the Prophet of God (ﷺ) was the Qur'an." The wording quoted by the author is also found in Ahmad 6/91, al-Bayhaqi 2/499, and al-Tabari 29/13.]]

Qatada said: it is what he used to carry out of God's command and refrain from of God's prohibition, and the meaning is: you are upon the character which God commanded you in the Qur'an.

It was also said: God called his character great because he complied with God's discipline of him in His saying: ﴿Take what is easy in forgiveness﴾ (al-A'raf 7:199), and so on.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verses 5–6:

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So you will see and they will see﴾: "So you will see, O Muhammad, and they will see" — meaning the people of Makkah — "when the punishment descends upon them."

﴿Which of you is the afflicted (al-maftun)?﴾ It has been said that its meaning is: "Which of you is the madman?" Thus "al-maftun" is a passive participle used in the sense of a verbal noun (masdar), as one says: "There is no being-flogged (majlud) or intellect (ma'qul) in so-and-so," meaning endurance (jaladah) and intellect ('aql). This is the meaning of the saying of al-Dahhak and the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

It has also been said that the ba' (bi-) is in the sense of "fi" (in), its metaphorical meaning being: "So you will see and they will see in which of the two groups the madman is: is it in your group or in theirs?"

It has also been said that the ba' is in the sense of "ma'" (with), and "al-maftun" is the Shaytan. [The meaning: with which of you is the Shaytan: with the believers or with the disbelievers?] [[What is between the brackets is from "b".]] This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid. [[In "b": Qatadah.]]

Others said: the ba' is extra (za'idah), and its meaning is: "Which of you is the afflicted?" That is, the madman who has been afflicted with madness. This is the saying of Qatadah.

Indeed your Lord knows best who has strayed from His path, and He knows best those who are guided. So do not obey the deniers (﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾), meaning the polytheists of Makkah, for they used to invite him to the religion of their forefathers, so He forbade him from obeying them.

﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ (﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾). Al-Dahhak said: "They wish you would disbelieve, so they would disbelieve." Al-Kalbi said: "They wish you would be lenient toward them, so they would be lenient toward you." Al-Hasan said: "They wish you would flatter them in your religion, so they would flatter you in their religion." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They wish you would be hypocritical and show off, so they would be hypocritical and show off." Ibn Qutaybah said: "They wanted you to worship their gods for a period, and they would worship God for a period."

﴿And do not obey every frequent swearer, contemptible one﴾ (﴿وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَهِينٍ﴾), one who swears often by falsehood. [Muqatil said: he means] [[In "A": it was said.]] al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. It was also said: al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth. And Ata' said: al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. ﴿Contemptible﴾ (mahin) means weak and despicable. It was said: it is a pattern (fa'il) derived from mahana (contemptibility), which is lack of judgment and discernment. Ibn Abbas said: a liar. This is close to the first, because a person lies only out of the contemptibility of his own self upon him.

﴿Defamer﴾ (hammaz): one who backbites, eating the flesh of people through slander and backbiting. Al-Hasan said: he is the one who insults his brother in the assembly, like the statement [of God], "hummazah" (a defamer). ﴿Walker with tale-bearing﴾ (mashsha' bi-namim): a gossiper who goes about among people with tale-bearing (namimah) in order to cause discord among them.

﴿Preventer of good﴾ (mannai lil-khayr): stingy with wealth. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verse 14:

﴿Because he has wealth and sons.﴾ Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub read "a-in" (ﺃَﺈِﻥْ) with the interrogative particle (istifham, interrogation). Then Hamzah and Abu Bakr lighten the two hamzahs without elongation (madd), while Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub elongate the first hamzah and soften the second. The others read it without the interrogative, as a statement (khabar). Whoever reads it with the interrogative, its meaning is: "Is it because he has wealth and sons?"

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verses 15–17:

﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ That is, he made the repayment of the blessings bestowed upon him, of sons and wealth, to be disbelief in Our verses. It is also said: its meaning is, "Because he possesses wealth and sons [do you obey him?]" [[In "B" it reads: "tughyihi" (you would transgress).]].

As for the one who recites it as a statement, its meaning is: do not obey every oft-swearing, contemptible man, because ﴿he possesses wealth and sons﴾ [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]]; that is, do not obey him for his wealth and his sons, ﴿when Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Tales of the ancients."﴾

Then He threatened him, saying: ﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾. "Al-khurtum" means the nose. Abu al-Aliyah and Mujahid said: that is, We will blacken his face, and We will make for him a mark in the Hereafter by which he will be recognized, and it is the blackness of the face.

Al-Farra' said: He singled out the snout for the branding, for it is in the sense of the face, since a part of a thing may be used to express the whole of it.

Ibn Abbas said: We will strike his snout with the sword, and this was indeed done to him on the day of Badr. [[Mentioned by al-Tabari: 29/28.]] Qatadah said: We will attach to him something that will not leave him.

Al-Qutaybi said: The Arabs say of a man who has been reviled with a foul insult: "He has branded him with an evil brand," meaning: he attached to him a shame that does not leave him, just as a brand's mark is not erased nor does its trace fade. And Allah attached to the defects He mentioned a shame that will not leave him in this world and the Hereafter, like the brand upon the snout.

Al-Dahhak and al-Kisa'i said: We will strike him upon his face.

﴿Indeed, We have tested them﴾, meaning: We tested the people of Makkah with drought and hunger, ﴿as We tested the companions of the garden﴾, i.e., We tried them. Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the companions of the garden," that he said: There was a garden in Yemen called al-Dhirwan, two farsakhs from San'a, which travellers would pass through. It had been planted by a people from the people of prayer. It belonged to a man who died, and three sons inherited it from him. Whenever the poor came to them after they had cut their palm trees, whatever the sickle passed over and did not cut was for the poor; and whatever fell from the top of the palm onto the mat was also for the poor; and when they harvested their crops, whatever the sickle passed over was for the poor, and when they threshed it, whatever was scattered was also for the poor. When the father died and these brothers inherited from their father, they said: "By Allah, the wealth is indeed little, and the dependents are indeed many. This practice was only followed when wealth was abundant and dependents few. As for now, when wealth is little and dependents many, we cannot do this." So they made a pact among themselves that one day they would set out at dawn, before the people went out, and cut their palm trees, and they did not make the exception, meaning they did not say "if Allah wills." So the people set out in the darkness of the night to their garden to cut it before the poor came out. They found it blackened, for a visitation of punishment had gone around it during the night and burned it, so it became like a cut-down field [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/311; al-Qurtubi: 18/239–240; Zad al-Masir: 8/335.]]. This is the meaning of His words, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿when they swore﴾, i.e., made oath, ﴿that they would surely cut its fruit at morning﴾, meaning they would surely harvest its fruit and cut it off when they woke in the morning, ﴿before the poor could know﴾.

﴿Then there swept over it a visitation﴾ — a punishment ﴿from your Lord﴾ — by night. The visitation only occurs at night. That visitation was a fire that descended from the sky and burned it, ﴿while they were sleeping﴾.

﴿So it became like the cut-down [garden]﴾ — like the pitch-dark, black night. Al-Hasan said: meaning the good was cut off from it, so there was nothing left in it.

Al-Akhfash said: "like the dawn cut off from the night." The root of "ṣarīm" is "maṣrūm" (cut off), like "qatīl" and "maqtūl." Everything that is cut off is ṣarīm, [so the night is ṣarīm][[Omitted from manuscript "a".]] and the dawn is ṣarīm, because each of them is cut off from the other.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "like black ashes," in the dialect of Khuzaymah.

﴿So they called out to one another in the morning﴾ — some of them called to others when they woke up in the morning.

﴿Go early to your tilth﴾ — meaning the fruits, the crops and the grapes — ﴿if you are going to harvest﴾ — cutting the palm trees.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verse 23–28:

﴿So they set off﴾ — they walked toward it — ﴿while they whispered to one another, "No needy person shall enter it today against you."﴾ — they conferred in secret, one saying to another in private. ﴿And they went early, with determination﴾. "Al-hard" (intent, restraint, anger) in the language may mean intention, prevention, or wrath. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "with diligence and effort."

Al-Qurazi, Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: "upon a matter agreed upon, which they had established among themselves." This is in the sense of intention, for the one who intends something (ilā al-shay', in "b" li-l-shay') is resolute and determined upon the matter.

Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutaybi said: they set out with the intention of withholding from the needy. It is said: "harada al-sanah" when there was no rain in the year, and "haradat al-naqah" when she had no milk.

al-Sha'bi and Sufyan said: "with resentment and anger toward the needy."

From Ibn 'Abbas, he said: "with power," ﴿capable﴾ in their own estimation over their garden and its fruits, with no one coming between them and it.

﴿So when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we have gone astray."﴾ That is, when they saw the garden burnt, they said, "Indeed, we have lost our way; we have strayed to the place of our garden; this is not our garden." Then some of them said: ﴿"Rather, we have been deprived."﴾ — we were deprived of its good and benefit by our withholding from the needy and our abandoning the exception.

﴿The most moderate of them said﴾ — the most just of them, the most intelligent and the best of them: ﴿"Did I not tell you, 'Why do you not glorify [God]?'"﴾ — "Why do you not make the exception?" He rebuked them for leaving out the exception in their saying, "They will surely harvest it in the morning." He called the exception "glorification" because it is an exaltation of God and an acknowledgment that no one has power over anything except by His will.

Abu Salih said: their exception was "Glory be to God." It was also said: "Why do you not glorify God and say 'Glory be to God' and thank Him for what He has given you?" It was also said: "Why do you not seek His forgiveness for your action?"

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verses 29–38:

﴿They said, "Glory be to our Lord!"﴾ They declared Him far above being unjust in what He did, and they acknowledged against themselves the wrongdoing, saying: ﴿Indeed, we were wrongdoers﴾ by withholding (from) the needy.

﴿Then they turned to one another, blaming each other﴾ — each of them blamed the others for withholding the rights of the needy. And they called out against themselves, crying "Woe to us!": ﴿They said, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors﴾ in withholding the right of the poor. Ibn Kaysan said: "We transgressed against the blessings of Allah, so we did not give thanks for them, and we did not do what our fathers had done before."

Then they returned to themselves and said: ﴿"Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange something better than it. Indeed, we turn toward our Lord (in hope)."﴾ ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: "It has reached me that these people were sincere, and Allah recognized their truthfulness, so He replaced it for them with a garden called al-Hayawan (the Living), in which there are grapes, of which a mule could carry a single cluster." [See: al-Bahr al-Muhit, 8/313.]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Such is the punishment﴾ — that is, as We did to them, so We do to whoever transgresses Our limits and opposes Our command. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.﴾ Then He informed of what He has prepared for the God-fearing, saying: ﴿Indeed, for the God-fearing with their Lord are Gardens of Bliss.﴾ The polytheists said: "We will be given better in the Hereafter than you are given." So Allah, refuting them, said: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge? Or do you have a Book﴾ sent down from Allah ﴿in which﴾ — in this Book — ﴿you study﴾, i.e., you read,

﴿that indeed for you in it﴾ — in that Book — ﴿is whatever you choose﴾, i.e., you select and desire.

Then the Lord of the worlds will come to them in the lowest form in which they had seen Him before. He will say: What are you waiting for? Let every nation follow what they used to worship. They will say: O our Lord, we parted from the people in this world when we were most in need of them, and we did not keep their company. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You; we do not associate anything with Allah, twice or thrice, until some of them almost turn back. He will say: Is there a sign between you and Him by which you recognise Him? They will say: Yes. Then He will uncover the shin, and no one who used to prostrate to Allah of his own accord will remain except that Allah permits him to prostrate. And no one who used to prostrate out of hypocrisy and show will remain except that Allah makes his back a single plate; whenever he tries to prostrate he falls on his back. Then they will raise their heads, and He will have changed into the form in which they saw Him the first time, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: You are our Lord. Then the bridge will be laid over Hell, and intercession will be permitted, and they will say: O Allah, grant safety, grant safety." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the bridge?" He said: "It is slippery and unstable, with hooks, grapples and thorns, like the thorny plant in Najd called al-Sa'dan. The believers will cross it like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, and like the finest race-horses and riding camels. Some will be saved and safe, some will be scratched and released, and some will be thrown into the Fire of Hell. When the believers have been delivered from the Fire, by Him in whose hand my soul is, none of you is more insistent in demanding a right from Allah than the believers on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in the Fire. They will say: Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray with us and perform Hajj. It will be said to them: Bring out those you recognise. Their forms will be forbidden to the Fire, and they will bring out a great number whom the Fire has seized up to the middle of their shins and to their knees. Then they will say: Our Lord, none remains in it of those You commanded us to bring out. He will say: Return, and whoever you find in his heart a weight of a dinar of good, bring him out. They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left none in it of those You commanded us to bring out. He will say: Return, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of half a dinar of good, bring him out. They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left none in it of those You commanded us to bring out. He will say: Return, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of an atom of good, bring him out. They will bring out a great number. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have left none in it who has any good of those You commanded us to bring out."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verse 43:

﴿With their eyes downcast﴾. This is because the believers raise their heads from prostration, and their faces are whiter than snow, while the faces of the disbelievers and the hypocrites turn black. ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾: the humiliation of regret and remorse will overwhelm them. ﴿And they used to be called to prostration﴾. Ibrahim al-Taymi said: this means to the obligatory prayer, with the call (adhan) and the iqama. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they used to hear "Hasten to success" (hayya 'ala al-falah) and would not respond. ﴿While they were sound﴾, healthy, yet they would not come to it. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By Allah, this verse was only revealed concerning those who lag behind from the congregations.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verse 44–52:

﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with those who deny the Qur'an, and let Me take care of them. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, do not occupy your heart with them [, entrust them to Me, for I will suffice you against them] [[In "B," "and entrust him" (wakkilhu)]]. [He said: a similar usage is "Leave Me with the one whom I created alone" (74:11), meaning, linguistically: do not occupy your heart with him; entrust him to Me, for I will repay him. A similar saying is a man's words: "Leave me and him," not that he has prevented him from it, but its interpretation is "entrust him to me, for I will take care of his affair."]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Gradually We will draw them on﴾ — We will seize them with punishment ﴿from where they do not know﴾. So they were punished on the day of Badr.

﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm. Or do you ask them for payment, so that they are burdened with debt? Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down? So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾: be patient with their harm, awaiting your Lord's decree. ﴿And be not like the companion of the fish﴾ in haste and impatience — he is Yunus ibn Matta ﴿when he called out﴾ to his Lord [in] [[In "B," "from"]] the belly of the fish ﴿while he was suppressing [his grief]﴾, filled with distress.

﴿Had not a favour from his Lord reached him﴾ — overtaken him — ﴿when He had mercy upon him and accepted his repentance, he would have been cast out onto the open plain﴾ — thrown into the wide space out of the belly of the fish ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, being censured and blamed for his sin [committing it] [[In "B," "from"]].

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾ — selected him ﴿and made him among the righteous.﴾

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad!" (51) And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ (52)

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾: The disbelievers wanted to afflict the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the evil eye, so a group of Quraysh looked at him and said, "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banu Asad, to the extent that a fat she-camel or cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it, then say, "O girl, take the measure and the dirhams and bring us some meat from this," and it would not depart before it fell dead and was slaughtered. [[See: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (509).]]

Al-Kalbi said: a man of the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then he would lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say, "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these today," and before long a group and number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to afflict the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the evil eye and do to him the same, but Allah protected His Prophet and revealed: "And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes." [[See: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (510).]] That is, "wa-yakadu" (and they almost), and the lam entered "li-yuzliqunaka" because of the position of "inna" (indeed). The people of Madina read "layazliqunaka" with a fatha on the ya', and the others with a damma, and both are dialects: it is said zalaqahu, yazlaquhu, zalaqan, and azlaqahu, yuzliquhu, izlaqan.

Ibn Abbas said: its meaning is: they would pierce you (yunfidhunaka); it is said zaliqa al-sahm when the arrow passed through.

Al-Suddi said: they would strike you with their eyes. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: they would harm you. It was also said: they would remove you.

Al-Kalbi said: they would throw you down. It was also said: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the Message.

Ibn Qutayba said: He does not mean that they strike you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye strikes what pleases him with his eye; rather He means that they look at you when you recite the Qur'an with an intense gaze of enmity and hatred, nearly bringing you down. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 68, verse 44–52:

﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse.﴾ That is: leave Me to deal with those who deny the Qur'an, and let Me take care of them. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, do not occupy your heart with them [, entrust them to Me, for I will suffice you against them] [[In "B," "and entrust him" (wakkilhu)]]. [He said: a similar usage is "Leave Me with the one whom I created alone" (74:11), meaning, linguistically: do not occupy your heart with him; entrust him to Me, for I will repay him. A similar saying is a man's words: "Leave me and him," not that he has prevented him from it, but its interpretation is "entrust him to me, for I will take care of his affair."]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Gradually We will draw them on﴾ — We will seize them with punishment ﴿from where they do not know﴾. So they were punished on the day of Badr.

﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm. Or do you ask them for payment, so that they are burdened with debt? Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down? So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾: be patient with their harm, awaiting your Lord's decree. ﴿And be not like the companion of the fish﴾ in haste and impatience — he is Yunus ibn Matta ﴿when he called out﴾ to his Lord [in] [[In "B," "from"]] the belly of the fish ﴿while he was suppressing [his grief]﴾, filled with distress.

﴿Had not a favour from his Lord reached him﴾ — overtaken him — ﴿when He had mercy upon him and accepted his repentance, he would have been cast out onto the open plain﴾ — thrown into the wide space out of the belly of the fish ﴿while he was blameworthy﴾, being censured and blamed for his sin [committing it] [[In "B," "from"]].

﴿So his Lord chose him﴾ — selected him ﴿and made him among the righteous.﴾

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad!" (51) And it is not but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ (52)

﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes﴾: The disbelievers wanted to afflict the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the evil eye, so a group of Quraysh looked at him and said, "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banu Asad, to the extent that a fat she-camel or cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it, then say, "O girl, take the measure and the dirhams and bring us some meat from this," and it would not depart before it fell dead and was slaughtered. [[See: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (509).]]

Al-Kalbi said: a man of the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then he would lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say, "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these today," and before long a group and number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to afflict the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the evil eye and do to him the same, but Allah protected His Prophet and revealed: "And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes." [[See: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (510).]] That is, "wa-yakadu" (and they almost), and the lam entered "li-yuzliqunaka" because of the position of "inna" (indeed). The people of Madina read "layazliqunaka" with a fatha on the ya', and the others with a damma, and both are dialects: it is said zalaqahu, yazlaquhu, zalaqan, and azlaqahu, yuzliquhu, izlaqan.

Ibn Abbas said: its meaning is: they would pierce you (yunfidhunaka); it is said zaliqa al-sahm when the arrow passed through.

Al-Suddi said: they would strike you with their eyes. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: they would harm you. It was also said: they would remove you.

Al-Kalbi said: they would throw you down. It was also said: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the Message.

Ibn Qutayba said: He does not mean that they strike you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye strikes what pleases him with his eye; rather He means that they look at you when you recite the Qur'an with an intense gaze of enmity and hatred, nearly bringing you down. [[See: al-Qurtubi, 2/178.]]

Al-Zajjaj said: that is, from the intensity of their enmity, they nearly, with their gaze of hatred, bring you down. This is used in Arabic speech; one says: "He looked at me with a look that nearly knocks me down, and a look that nearly devours me." What confirms the soundness of this meaning is that He linked this gaze to hearing the Qur'an, saying: ﴿when they hear the Reminder﴾, and they were extremely averse to that, so they fixed their gaze upon him with hatred. ﴿And they say, "Indeed, he is mad!"﴾ — that is, they attribute madness to him when they hear him recite the Qur'an. So Allah, exalted is He, said:

﴿And it is not but﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿a reminder to the worlds.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: an admonition for the believers. Al-Hasan said: the remedy for being struck by the evil eye is that a person recite this verse. [[Mentioned by the author of al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/318.]]
